title: Starting Up a Project in Context

header.html: 4.1.1 carry out starting up a project: activities, inputs and outputs; recommended roles and responsibilities; how the practices are applied; 4.1.2 analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, using the purpose and objectives, the practices and tailoring
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

html:
1Purpose, objectives and context

The starting up a project process makes sure the prerequisites for initiation are in place. It answers one question: do we have a viable and worthwhile project? It is deliberately short. It happens before the project proper and ends with a decision by the project board.

In plain words, the objectives are:

  • A reason to do the project, shown in an outline business case.
  • The executive and project manager appointed, and the project management team designed.
  • Lessons from earlier work reviewed.
  • A delivery approach chosen, and a project brief that gives the board enough to decide.
  • The initiation stage planned.

The process serves ensure continued business justification (the outline case), learn from experience (previous lessons), define roles, responsibilities and relationships (the team), manage by stages (the board authorizes the initiation stage first) and tailor to suit the project.

Exam tip

. Starting up asks "is it worth initiating?", not "how will we deliver everything?" It needs an outline business case and a plan for the initiation stage only.

2Activities, inputs and outputs

Activity names below are given in general terms. The Official Book's wording may differ slightly, so learn what each activity achieves.

Activity What it achieves
Appoint the executive and the project manager The people who lead are named, so accountability exists from the start
Capture previous lessons Lessons from similar work are reviewed and the lessons log is started
Design and appoint the project management team Business, user and supplier interests are represented; board, assurance and support roles are identified
Prepare the outline business case The reason, expected benefits, rough cost and time, and options, in outline
Select the project approach and assemble the project brief The way of delivering, such as linear, iterative or hybrid, and the brief for the board
Plan the initiation stage The initiation stage plan: the work to produce the PID, with cost, time and tolerances
Direction Items
Inputs The trigger or project mandate; lessons from earlier projects; corporate standards and guidance; programme information, if any
Outputs The project brief with the outline business case; the initiation stage plan; the appointed roles; a started project log; the request for the board to authorize initiation
Exam tip

. The outputs of starting up are the project brief and the initiation stage plan. The PID is not one of them; it is produced in initiating. If an option has a detailed baseline in start-up, it belongs to initiating.

3Roles and responsibilities

The Official Book gives a table of who is responsible, accountable, consulted and informed for each activity (the RACI table). Responsible means does the work. Accountable means answers for the result. Consulted gives input. Informed is told. Learn each role's focus and check the book's table.

Role Focus in starting up
Corporate or programme management Provides the trigger or project mandate; makes sure the executive is appointed
Executive Accountable for the outline business case and for getting the right team in place
Senior user Brings the user need, and confirms users can commit people and time
Senior supplier Brings the supplier view of the approach and what can be delivered
Project manager Does much of the work: captures lessons, drafts the brief, plans the initiation stage, helps design the team
Project assurance Independently checks the brief and the proposed team
Project support Sets up the project log, filing and records
Exam tip

. Doing the work is not the same as being accountable. The project manager may draft the outline business case, but the executive is accountable for it.

4How the practices are applied

Practice Applied in starting up
Business case The outline business case in the project brief: reason, benefits, options
Organization The executive and project manager are appointed; the team is designed to cover all three interests
Plans The initiation stage plan; the project approach; an outline of the project product
Quality The customer's quality expectations and acceptance criteria are noted in the brief
Risk First risks and the risk appetite are noted; the risk register is started
Issues Early issues are captured; the issue register is started
Progress Tolerances for the initiation stage; the daily log and lessons log are started
Exam tip

. In start-up each practice is applied lightly and in outline. Detailed approaches, a full plan and a final business case belong to initiating.

5Judging the process

What effective start-up looks like Red flag, with the principle
An executive with real authority, budget and time A junior or unavailable executive (define roles)
A team that covers the business, user and supplier interests Only the supplier is represented; no senior user (define roles)
Previous lessons reviewed and used Lessons ignored because "this project is unique" (learn from experience)
An outline business case that is honest and enough to decide No case at all, or a detailed case that is really initiating work (business justification)
A brief and initiation stage plan that are short and clear Design or buying starts before the board authorizes initiation (manage by stages)
Initiation tolerances agreed with the board The project manager carries on with no stage tolerance (manage by exception)
Project manager independent of assurance Project manager also assures their own work (define roles)

Tailoring scales the process, but does not remove it.

Setting How start-up changes
Small internal project A two-page brief and a short initiation stage plan; one meeting to authorize initiation
Agile or hybrid delivery The approach names the iteration pattern and who speaks for users; the brief stays outline
Project in a programme The mandate comes from the programme and the brief reuses its information
Sustainability concerns Sustainability aims are noted in the outline business case
Exam tip

. Tailoring shortens start-up but never skips the decision. A small project still needs a justified reason, a named executive and a board decision to initiate.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Before the board decides on initiation of Project Harbor, Sam Okafor, the project manager, produces detailed estimates, a full risk analysis and the quality management approach. Was this an appropriate action, and why?

  • AYes, because the board cannot decide on initiation without a complete and detailed plan
  • BYes, because starting the build later is cheaper when every approach is already written
  • CNo, because start-up needs only an outline business case and an initiation stage plan
  • DNo, because the approaches may only be written once the build supplier has been chosen
Show the answer

Answer: C. Starting up needs just enough information for the board to decide on initiation, while detailed approaches and estimates are produced in initiating.

S2Sam Okafor drafted the outline business case for Project Harbor from the project mandate. Who is accountable for the outline business case?

  • AThe project manager, Sam Okafor
  • BThe senior user, Tomas Reyes
  • CProject assurance, Aisha Bello
  • DThe executive, Marta Quinn
Show the answer

Answer: D. The executive is accountable for the business case, even when the project manager does much of the drafting.

S3While capturing lessons for Project Harbor, Sam finds that a permit project at another port overran because users were engaged too late. What should Sam do?

  • ARecord the lesson in the lessons log and use it to shape the team and the approach
  • BLeave the lesson until the end project report, because lessons are reviewed at closure
  • CRecord it as a risk in the risk register and take no further action in start-up
  • DPass it to the supplier so Delta Software can adjust its own delivery plan
Show the answer

Answer: A. Capturing previous lessons is a start-up activity, and applying them to the team design and approach is the learn from experience principle in action.

S4Marta Quinn wants the board to decide whether to authorize initiation of Project Harbor. Which management product gives the board the outline business case, the project approach and the proposed team?

  • AThe PID, which sets out the detailed approaches and the baselined project plan
  • BThe project brief, which holds the outline business case, the approach and the team
  • CThe project product description, which sets out the acceptance criteria for the product
  • DThe benefits management approach, which sets out how and when benefits are measured
Show the answer

Answer: B. The project brief is the start-up output that lets the board decide on initiation, while the PID is produced during initiating.

S5A small internal Brightwater project to replace staff laptops has one user group. Sam used a two-page project brief and a short initiation stage plan, and one board meeting authorized initiation. Was this an appropriate action, and why?

  • ANo, because every project needs a full project brief of the same size and detail
  • BYes, because small projects need no business case or board decision to initiate
  • CNo, because initiation can only be authorized in a meeting that includes the supplier
  • DYes, because the process was scaled down but the board still had a justified case
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tailoring scales start-up down, but the board still needs a justified reason and a plan for initiation to decide on.

S6For Project Harbor, Sam's draft team has Marta Quinn, Lena Kovac and a user representative who has no authority over harbor operations. What should Sam do?

  • AAccept the user representative and ask the board to confirm the choice later
  • BAppoint Lena Kovac as senior user as well as senior supplier on the board
  • CPropose Tomas Reyes, the harbor master, as a senior user able to commit users
  • DDrop the user interest from the team because the supplier knows the permit process
Show the answer

Answer: C. The senior user must speak for the user interest with authority to commit people and decide, as Tomas Reyes does for harbor operations.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What question does starting up a project answer?

Show the answer

Do we have a viable and worthwhile project?

R2What is the trigger for starting up a project?

Show the answer

The project mandate or trigger from the corporate, programme or customer level.

R3Name the two main outputs.

Show the answer

The project brief and the initiation stage plan.

R4Which business case exists after starting up?

Show the answer

The outline business case, held in the project brief.

R5In a responsibility table, what does accountable mean?

Show the answer

Answers for the result of the activity.

R6Which log is started in start-up to hold earlier and new lessons?

Show the answer

The lessons log.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose prerequisites for initiation; a viable and worthwhile project?
Inputs trigger or project mandate, earlier lessons, standards
Outputs project brief, initiation stage plan, appointed roles
Activities appoint, learn, design the team, outline case, approach and brief, plan initiation
Accountability the executive for the case; the project manager does much of the work
Practices applied lightly and in outline
Red flags weak executive, missing interest, detailed work too early
